subject: Request: Amend streaming vs sync throughput commitments (first-burst / sustained) — Brightlane
messages:
From: Evan Liu <eng@brightlane.ai>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@saasops.com
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA ask: first-burst vs sustained token commitments for streaming endpoints

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're excited about Redwood's streaming API — low-latency output is critical for our product. Before we move forward we'd like to request an amendment to the proposed SLA to cover two real-world modes of traffic we see: short, high-concurrency bursts (live chat spikes during product launches) and long-running steady streams (background summarization jobs).

Specifically:
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT): for interactive streams we need the first token to start arriving within 250–350 ms for the 95th percentile.
- First-burst window: during the first 2 seconds of a spike, we expect the system to deliver up to 120 tokens total across a user's request (we typically see 40 tokens/user * up to 3 concurrent streams per user during launch traffic).
- Sustained throughput: after the initial 2s window, we expect the stream to maintain ~20 tokens/sec per connection for normal streams (and lower for background jobs).

We understand these are aggressive. We're open to a pilot or dedicated pool but we need contractual language that allows us to rely on these numbers (or get credits/backstop) because customers measure perceived latency and it impacts conversion. Attached is a small trace of our peak behavior (token_profile_trace.csv).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept an explicit carveout in the SLA that defines a "first-burst" tier, and what the fallback / credit model would look like if those burst guarantees are missed?

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call.

—Evan
Evan Liu
Head of Platform Engineering
Brightlane Analytics

[attachment: token_profile_trace.csv]

From: soojin.lee@redwood.com
To: Evan Liu <eng@brightlane.ai>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA ask: first-burst vs sustained token commitments for streaming endpoints

Evan — thanks for the clear profile and the trace. We're glad Brightlane liked the demo.

High-level response: we can define a "first-burst" carveout in the commercial SLA, but the exact numeric commitments need to balance:

- predictable TTFT at scale (depends on routing + KV cache warmup),
- per-GPU token emission capacity, and
- whether Brightlane needs a dedicated capacity pool.

Proposed immediate path:
1) Pilot a dedicated pool for peak traffic (isolates capacity and makes commitments concrete).
2) For the pilot, commit to a pragmatic baseline: 95th percentile TTFT <= 400 ms and first-burst delivery of 80 tokens within the first 2s per active stream (we can tighten this based on pilot telemetry).
3) Sustained: guarantee 20 tokens/sec per stream as a target for the dedicated pool, with documented throttling rules and graceful degradation/fallback to a sync endpoint if necessary.

Next steps: I'll loop in Karthik (engineering) to confirm feasibility and Marissa for commercial signoff on the pilot discount. If you're open, can we schedule a 30-min scoping call later this week?

Thanks,

— Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: soojin.lee@redwood.com, Evan Liu <eng@brightlane.ai>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA ask: first-burst vs sustained token commitments for streaming endpoints

Evan / Soojin — quick technical readout from infra side.

Thanks for the trace. A few things to set expectations and make commitments measurable:

1) TTFT drivers: network egress + routing to hot GPU + model kv cache warmup. For small prompts our production numbers (multi-tenant hosted) show 95p TTFT ~300–450 ms depending on region and burstiness. We can hit ~250–300 ms when traffic is pinned to a dedicated pool and prefix caching is warmed.

2) First-burst semantics: we suggest defining "first-burst" as the first 2s after connection open. In a dedicated pool, we can target delivering 100 tokens within that 2s window for up to 50 concurrent streams (this assumes prefilling and aggressive micro-batching). For multi-tenant hosted pools numbers will be lower.

3) Sustained throughput: token emission per connection is limited by model decode speed and GPU token throughput. Empirically, for the models under consideration we can maintain 15–25 tokens/sec per stream on dedicated A100-like capacity; wide variance if you use quantized variants.

4) Telemetry: we'll emit TTFT and token/sec metrics per request (trace id) during the pilot. That telemetry will be the basis for SLAs and credit calculations.

I'll attach the token_profile_trace.csv annotated with expected kernel-level bottlenecks. If Brightlane confirms dedicated pool + pilot, engineering can scope capacity and an ops runbook for warmup/caching prefetch.

— Karthik
Principal Engineer, Redwood Inference

[attachment: token_profile_trace.csv]

From: Marta Gomez <marta.gomez@brightlane.ai>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Evan Liu <eng@brightlane.ai>, procurement@saasops.com
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Brightlane counter-proposal and draft redlines

Soojin / Karthik — thanks for the quick replies. Procurement has reviewed and here's what they'd like to see in the commercial amendment (high level):

- Availability: 99.9% availability for the dedicated streaming pool during business hours (US PST), with defined maintenance windows.
- First Token: 95th percentile TTFT <= 250 ms for interactive streams.
- First-burst: deliver >= 120 tokens within the first 2s for interactive sessions for up to 30 concurrent priority connections.
- Credits: for misses against First Token or First-burst metrics, apply service credits scaled to the severity and frequency (we can start with a 5% monthly credit per missed SLA instance, capped at 50%).
- Dedicated pool: Brightlane requires the option to use a dedicated pool for the first 12 months of the contract, with a migration/fallback plan back to multi-tenant hosted offering.

We attached a redlined Word doc with suggested contract language. We understand some items are operationally challenging; please identify which items you can accept as-is, which need modification, and which must be scoped via the pilot.

Link to DocuSign (procurement wants to move quickly): https://docusign.example/brightlane/slas

Regards,
Marta
VP, Procurement — Brightlane Analytics

[attachment: Brightlane_SLA_redline.docx]

From: soojin.lee@redwood.com
To: Marta Gomez <marta.gomez@brightlane.ai>, Evan Liu <eng@brightlane.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Brightlane counter-proposal and draft redlines

Marta / Evan — appreciate the clarity and the redlines. Internal summary and next steps below: 

Summary:
- We can offer a pilot on a dedicated pool to validate tighter TTFT and first-burst numbers. Engineering feels the following is realistic for pilot: 95p TTFT <= 300–350 ms, first-burst >= 100 tokens in first 2s for up to 40 concurrent priority streams, sustained ~20 tokens/sec per stream.
- Brightlane's ask for 250 ms TTFT and 120 tokens in 2s for 30 streams is aggressive but likely achievable after a short optimization phase (prefill + warmup).
- Credits: we can accept a structured credit model tied to pilot telemetry; final percentages to be confirmed by Marissa (commercial).

Action items:
- Karthik & ops to propose pilot capacity and runbook (warmup hooks, prefetch API).
- Marissa to confirm commercial terms and pilot discount threshold; internal approval for dedicated pool cost.
- Soojin to schedule a 60-min scoping call with Brightlane + eng this week.

If everyone agrees I'll propose times for the scoping call and a draft pilot SOW. Once pilot telemetry validates the numbers we'll turn the successful metrics into binding SLA language.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this.

— Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
